derivation: from G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G473 (ἀντί);

occurrences.text: And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying, All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him.
And when he was come out of the ship, immediately there met him out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit,
And he sendeth forth two of his disciples, and saith unto them, Go ye into the city, and there shall meet you a man bearing a pitcher of water: follow him.
Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand?
And as he entered into a certain village, there met him ten men that were lepers, which stood afar off:
And as he was now going down, his servants met him, and told him, saying, Thy son liveth.
And it came to pass, as we went to prayer, a certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination met us, which brought her masters much gain by soothsaying:
